question: What do we call glands that release their secretions directly into the bloodstream without using ducts?
explanation: Endocrine glands do not have ducts to carry their secretions, releasing hormones straight into nearby blood vessels instead. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is it important for midwives to understand the endocrine system when caring for pregnant women?

options.A: Hormones produced by endocrine glands are only active during the first trimester of gestation
options.B: The endocrine system operates completely independently of the reproductive system during pregnancy
options.C: Midwives spend most of their training performing surgical removal of diseased endocrine organs
options.D: Pregnancy and childbirth involve massive hormonal shifts that regulate labor and postpartum recovery

explanation: Maternal adaptations and the actual process of labor rely heavily on coordinated hormone releases from multiple glands. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h1)

question: In which bony structure of the skull does the pituitary gland sit?
explanation: The sella turcica is a saddle-shaped depression in the sphenoid bone that houses and protects the pituitary gland. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the main difference between the front (anterior) and back (posterior) lobes of the pituitary gland?

options.A: The posterior lobe controls basal metabolic rate, while the anterior lobe regulates only uterine contractions
options.B: The posterior lobe produces oxytocin independently, while the anterior lobe has no endocrine function
options.C: The anterior lobe synthesizes its own hormones, while the posterior lobe stores and releases hypothalamic hormones
options.D: The anterior lobe connects directly to the optic chiasm, while the posterior lobe sits outside the skull

explanation: Oxytocin and ADH are manufactured in the hypothalamus and simply stored and released by the posterior pituitary, unlike anterior hormones. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h2)

question: Where are the parathyroid glands located in relation to the thyroid gland?

options.A: Inside the central isthmus of the thyroid
options.B: On the posterior surface of the thyroid lobes
options.C: Deep within the cartilage of the larynx
options.D: Superior to the hyoid bone in the upper neck

explanation: Usually numbering four, the small parathyroid glands are embedded or attached directly to the back of the thyroid gland lobes. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h3)

question: If the parathyroid glands are accidentally damaged or removed during thyroid surgery, what immediate problem is the patient at risk of developing?

options.A: Severe low blood calcium leading to muscle tetany
options.B: Sudden enlargement of the anterior pituitary gland
options.C: Uncontrollable spikes in maternal blood pressure
options.D: Complete cessation of all thyroid hormone production

explanation: Parathyroid hormone controls calcium levels; losing these glands causes blood calcium to drop dangerously low, affecting nerve and muscle function. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h3)

question: In which part of the abdomen are the adrenal glands located?
explanation: The adrenal glands sit directly on top of the kidneys, placing them behind the peritoneal lining in the retroperitoneal space. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the hormones produced by the adrenal cortex?

options.A: Supporting metabolic processes alongside other endocrine organs
options.B: Regulating salt and water balance through mineralocorticoids
options.C: Helping the body manage physical and emotional stress via cortisol
options.D: Triggering the rapid fight-or-flight response during sudden fright

explanation: The fight-or-flight response is mediated by adrenaline and noradrenaline, which are secreted by the inner adrenal medulla, not the cortex. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h4)

question: What are the tiny clusters of hormone-producing cells scattered throughout the pancreas called?
explanation: The endocrine pancreas is made up of these tiny cell clusters containing alpha and beta cells that regulate blood sugar. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why is the pancreas considered a mixed or dual-purpose gland?

options.A: It produces hormones that affect both the anterior pituitary and the adrenal cortex
options.B: It has both exocrine tissue for digestion and endocrine tissue for hormone release
options.C: It functions independently during pregnancy but requires the liver to work postpartum
options.D: It is located partially inside the peritoneal cavity and partially within the skull

explanation: The pancreas secretes digestive enzymes via ducts (exocrine) and hormones directly into the blood (endocrine). [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h5)

question: Where are the female ovaries typically located?

options.A: Attached directly to the posterior pituitary gland
options.B: In the pelvic cavity lateral to the uterus
options.C: Within the anterior neck inferior to the larynx
options.D: In the retroperitoneal space above the kidneys

explanation: The ovaries sit on either side of the uterus in the true pelvis, securely held by supportive ligaments. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why are the male testes located outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.A: To maintain a lower temperature required for healthy sperm production
options.B: To ensure the rapid synthesis of adrenal cortex steroid hormones
options.C: To allow direct connection with the exocrine ducts of the pancreas
options.D: To protect the pelvic organs from the pressure of the growing uterus

explanation: Scrotal placement keeps the testes slightly cooler than core body temperature, which is essential for spermatogenesis. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which major endocrine gland is situated in the front of the neck just below the voice box?
explanation: The thyroid gland wraps around the front of the trachea in the lower neck, just under the larynx. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h7)

question: A pregnant client is diagnosed with gestational diabetes. Which organ and hormone system are primarily involved in this condition?

options.A: Posterior pituitary and its blocked oxytocin release
options.B: Pancreas and its inadequate insulin production
options.C: Adrenal cortex and its deficient cortisol output
options.D: Thyroid gland and its excess thyroxine secretion

explanation: Gestational diabetes involves problems with blood sugar regulation tied to insulin produced by the endocrine pancreas. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h7)
